definition: A generation strategy that produces multiple candidate outputs for the same prompt and selects the best one according to some scoring criterion.
details: Best-of-N sampling trades additional inference compute for improved output quality, and is often combined with a reward model or verifier to automatically select the most promising candidate from the generated set.
story: Think of a jazz musician who has heard so many solos that a new one simply falls out of their fingers. In plain words: A generation strategy that produces multiple candidate outputs for the same prompt and selects the best one according to some scoring criterion. Here is how it actually plays out: Best-of-N sampling trades additional inference compute for improved output quality, and is often combined with a reward model or verifier to automatically select the most promising candidate from the generated set. Creation, here, is memory recombined at speed. That next-word, next-stroke magic is Best-of-N Sampling.
